findings.summary: The only committed acceptance evidence belongs to a different development: .dd-evidence/acceptance.json carries development_id dev_ledr_s1b_cas_hardening_02, input_commit 4f26fecd9ce227edf4b6d4b29480c0188913179b, and a test run of 26 tests across cas/protocol/bus only, so it does not evidence this package's B12 (npm run typecheck and npm test exit 0) — its run predates test/tick.test.ts. I reached this independently of the Continuous note; my own static review of src/tick.ts and test/tick.test.ts against tsconfig.json (strict, include [src, test], no noUnusedParameters) found no type or logic error that would fail either command, and the acceptance stage regenerates this evidence, so this is informational only.

The B1 purity guard is slightly weaker than the spec's stated grep: it matches /new\s+Date/, so a clock read written as Date.now() would pass the assertion while violating spec §7 B1 ("函数体内无 fetch / Date / Math.random，grep 零命中"). src/tick.ts is currently clean of all three, so this is an assertion-power gap in the guard, not a defect in the delivered decideTick.

decideTick derives the in-flight count from the pre-reclaim board snapshot, so worker slots freed by reclaim decisions emitted earlier in the same tick are not reused until the next tick. This is self-consistent (the open list is likewise taken from the snapshot) and strictly conservative — it can only under-dispatch, never exceed maxConcurrentWorkers — but a literal reading of spec §4 after §3's reclaim step would free those slots immediately.

The closed-enum sources check runs only over open cards reached before the dispatch budget n is exhausted, and the loop breaks on dispatched >= n before inspecting the remainder. A card with out-of-enum sources sitting past the budget (or any bad card when n <= 0) is therefore not moved to blocked until a later tick has capacity. Spec §4 places the validation inside the dispatch step, so this is consistent with the spec and B8 holds as written (1 blocked + 2 dispatched); noting it because the blocked outcome is capacity-dependent rather than immediate.

Spec §8 requires per-assertion attribution of the N1-N6 mutation self-check, and §9 permits that running evidence to live in the commit message and/or a new package-local file. No tracked file in the subject tree carries such attribution, and my read-only file inspection cannot read commit message bodies, so I can neither confirm nor refute that the evidence was recorded there. I verified the attribution mechanically instead by reading the guards: B3 (conflict stub, spawn count 0) kills N2, B4 (shared seq, casIdx < spawnIdx) kills N1 and is the non-degenerate stub §8.1 demands, B5 (throwing spawn, rollback CAS to open) kills N3, B7 (in-flight 3 / open 5 / max 4 => 1) kills N4, B8 kills N5, and B9's proposed=3 case kills N6.
